**JOINT DEFENSE AGREEMENT**

Prepared by Pryor Whitfield LLP on behalf of Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC

Circulated: May 2, 2025

Requested Return of Executed Counterparts by: May 23, 2025

**JOINT DEFENSE AGREEMENT**

This Joint Defense Agreement (this \"Agreement\") is entered into as of the last date of execution set forth on the signature pages hereto (the \"Effective Date\"), by and among:

> \(1\) **Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC**, a Delaware limited liability company (\"Kerrigan-Holst\");
>
> \(2\) **Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc.**, a Delaware corporation (\"Vantage\");
>
> \(3\) **Stonebridge Components Corp.**, an Ohio corporation (\"Stonebridge\"); and
>
> \(4\) **TerraForge Precision, Inc.**, a Texas corporation (\"TerraForge\").

Each of Kerrigan-Holst, Vantage, Stonebridge, and TerraForge is referred to herein individually as a \"Party\" and collectively as the \"Parties.\"

**RECITALS**

**WHEREAS**, the Parties are named defendants in the matter captioned *In re Industrial Fasteners Antitrust Litigation*, Case No. 1:23-cv-04871, pending before the Honorable Margaret R. Tanaka in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois (the \"Litigation\");

**WHEREAS**, the Consolidated Purchasers Class, purporting to act on behalf of direct purchasers of industrial fasteners, has asserted claims against the Parties under Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1, and Section 4 of the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. § 15, seeking, among other relief, treble damages, injunctive relief, attorneys\' fees, and costs (the \"Claims\");

**WHEREAS**, the Parties believe that they share common legal interests in defending against the Claims asserted in the Litigation and that coordination of their respective defenses will serve those common interests and promote the efficient and effective resolution of the Litigation;

**WHEREAS**, the Parties wish to enter into this Agreement to facilitate the exchange of information, defense strategies, and legal analyses among them and their respective counsel in furtherance of their common defense, while preserving all applicable privileges, immunities, and protections, including the attorney-client privilege, the work-product doctrine, and the joint defense privilege (also known as the common-interest doctrine); and

**WHEREAS**, the Parties and their respective counsel, as identified on Schedule A attached hereto and incorporated herein by reference, have been requested to execute this Agreement and return executed counterparts to counsel for Kerrigan-Holst no later than May 23, 2025.

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements set forth herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the Parties agree as follows:

**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS]{.underline}**

As used in this Agreement, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below:

**Section 1.1 --- \"Agreement.\"** \"Agreement\" means this Joint Defense Agreement, including all schedules and exhibits attached hereto, as the same may be amended, supplemented, or modified from time to time in accordance with the terms hereof.

**Section 1.2 --- \"Common Defense.\"** \"Common Defense\" means the defense of the Parties against the Claims asserted in the Litigation and any Related Proceeding, including, without limitation, the coordination of defense strategy, the sharing of information, and the joint retention of experts, consultants, and vendors in furtherance thereof.

**Section 1.3 --- \"Counsel.\"** \"Counsel\" means the outside law firms and in-house legal personnel representing each Party in connection with the Litigation and any Related Proceeding, as set forth on Schedule A hereto. The designation of Counsel on Schedule A may be amended from time to time by written notice from the applicable Party to all other Parties and their Counsel, in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 12.2 of this Agreement.

**Section 1.4 --- \"Joint Defense Material.\"** \"Joint Defense Material\" means all information, documents, communications, memoranda, analyses, legal theories, expert reports and analyses, factual summaries, interview notes, chronologies, draft pleadings, and other materials of any kind or nature shared among or between the Parties or their Counsel pursuant to this Agreement, whether in written, electronic, oral, or other form, and whether or not such materials are marked or designated as confidential or privileged at the time of disclosure.

**Section 1.5 --- \"Litigation.\"** \"Litigation\" means the matter captioned *In re Industrial Fasteners Antitrust Litigation*, Case No. 1:23-cv-04871, pending in the United States District Court for the Northern District of Illinois before the Honorable Margaret R. Tanaka, including all proceedings, motions, discovery, hearings, trials, appeals, and related matters arising therefrom or in connection therewith.

**Section 1.6 --- \"Related Proceeding.\"** \"Related Proceeding\" means any investigation, inquiry, proceeding, or action by any federal, state, or local governmental or regulatory agency or authority concerning the same or substantially similar subject matter as the Litigation, including, without limitation, any investigation by the Antitrust Division of the United States Department of Justice, any state attorney general, or any other governmental body.

**Section 1.7 --- \"Steering Committee.\"** \"Steering Committee\" means the Joint Defense Steering Committee established pursuant to Article VI of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE II --- SCOPE OF JOINT DEFENSE]{.underline}**

**Section 2.1 --- Scope.** The joint defense established by this Agreement shall encompass all matters arising out of or relating to the Litigation and any Related Proceeding (collectively, the \"Joint Defense Matters\"). The Parties agree to cooperate in the Common Defense to the extent consistent with their respective individual interests. The scope of this Agreement is intended to be coextensive with the claims, allegations, and subject matter at issue in the Litigation, including all factual and legal issues raised therein, and shall extend to any Related Proceeding that may arise during the pendency of this Agreement.

**Section 2.2 --- Common Interest.** The Parties acknowledge and agree that they share a common legal interest in defending against the Claims asserted in the Litigation and that this Agreement is entered into to advance that common legal interest. The Parties further acknowledge that the common interest among them is sufficient to support the application of the joint defense privilege (also known as the common-interest doctrine) to communications and materials exchanged pursuant to this Agreement, and that the Parties intend for all such communications and materials to be protected by such privilege to the fullest extent permitted by applicable law.

**Section 2.3 --- No Limitation on Individual Defense.** Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to prevent, limit, or restrict any Party from presenting its own individual defense in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding, including, without limitation, asserting defenses, filing motions, conducting discovery, retaining experts, or taking any other action in furtherance of its individual defense, provided that such individual defense does not involve the unauthorized use or disclosure of Joint Defense Material received from another Party. Each Party expressly reserves all rights, defenses, claims, and counterclaims available to it in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding, whether or not such rights, defenses, claims, or counterclaims are consistent with the positions of the other Parties.

**[ARTICLE III --- PRIVILEGE AND CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- Joint Defense Privilege.** The Parties intend that the sharing of Joint Defense Material pursuant to this Agreement is protected by the joint defense privilege (also known as the common-interest doctrine) as recognized under federal common law and applicable state law. The disclosure of Joint Defense Material by one Party to another Party or to such other Party\'s Counsel shall not constitute a waiver of the attorney-client privilege, the work-product protection established under Rule 26(b)(3) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure, or any other applicable privilege, immunity, or protection. The Parties intend that all Joint Defense Material shall retain its privileged and protected status as though such material had not been disclosed to any other Party or its Counsel, and the Parties shall take all reasonable steps to preserve and maintain such privileges and protections.

**Section 3.2 --- Confidentiality Designation.** All Joint Defense Material shared under this Agreement in written or electronic form shall be marked or designated with the legend \"Joint Defense Material --- Privileged and Confidential\" or words of substantially similar import. Oral communications shared during joint defense meetings, telephone calls, videoconferences, or other discussions among the Parties or their Counsel shall be deemed designated as Joint Defense Material without the need for marking or other formality. The failure to mark or designate any particular communication or document shall not affect its status as Joint Defense Material if such communication or document was shared pursuant to this Agreement and in furtherance of the Common Defense.

**Section 3.3 --- Use Restriction.** Joint Defense Material shall be used solely for purposes of the Common Defense and shall not be used for any other purpose, including, without limitation, any commercial, competitive, or business purpose. Joint Defense Material shall not be disclosed to any person or entity other than:

> \(a\) Counsel for a Party, including attorneys, paralegals, legal assistants, and other professional staff at the law firms identified on Schedule A who are directly involved in the Common Defense;
>
> \(b\) employees, officers, directors, or agents of a Party who have a need to know the contents of such Joint Defense Material in connection with the Common Defense, provided that any such person is advised of the confidential and privileged nature of the material prior to receiving access thereto; and
>
> \(c\) experts, consultants, or vendors retained in connection with the Common Defense who have executed a confidentiality undertaking in a form reasonably acceptable to the disclosing Party prior to receiving access to any Joint Defense Material.

**Section 3.4 --- No Disclosure to Third Parties.** No Party or its Counsel shall disclose Joint Defense Material to any third party, including, without limitation, any opposing party, any plaintiff or plaintiff\'s counsel in the Litigation, any governmental agency or regulatory authority, any co-defendant that is not a Party to this Agreement, or any other person or entity not authorized to receive such material under Section 3.3 of this Agreement, without the prior written consent of the Party that provided such material. In the event that a Party or its Counsel is served with a subpoena, court order, discovery request, or other legal process that compels or purports to compel the disclosure of Joint Defense Material, the receiving Party shall:

> \(i\) provide prompt written notice to the disclosing Party of such subpoena, court order, or legal process, and in no event later than five (5) business days after receipt thereof;
>
> \(ii\) cooperate with the disclosing Party in any effort to obtain a protective order, quash the subpoena, or obtain other appropriate relief to prevent or limit such disclosure; and
>
> \(iii\) disclose only such Joint Defense Material as is strictly required by the applicable court order, subpoena, or legal process, after exhausting all reasonable avenues to prevent or limit such disclosure.

**Section 3.5 --- No Obligation to Share Work Product.** Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to require any Party to share its own attorney work product, legal analyses, mental impressions, conclusions, opinions, or legal theories with any other Party. Each Party retains sole and absolute discretion over whether and to what extent it will share such materials with other Parties. The decision by any Party not to share particular work product shall not be deemed a breach of this Agreement or a failure to cooperate in the Common Defense.

**[ARTICLE IV --- INFORMATION SHARING]{.underline}**

**Section 4.1 --- Obligation to Share Non-Work-Product Materials.** Each Party agrees to share with the other Parties, through the Steering Committee or directly as the Steering Committee may direct, all non-work-product materials relevant to the Common Defense within ten (10) business days of a request from the Steering Committee. For purposes of this Section 4.1, \"non-work-product materials\" include, without limitation, factual documents and records, data and databases, deposition transcripts and exhibits, written discovery responses (including interrogatory answers, responses to requests for admission, and responses to requests for production of documents), correspondence with opposing counsel, correspondence with the Court, and any other materials relevant to the Litigation that do not constitute attorney work product.

**Section 4.2 --- Requests for Information.** Requests for information sharing under this Article IV shall be made in writing by or through the Steering Committee to Counsel for the applicable Party. The Steering Committee may establish reasonable procedures governing the format, manner, timing, and sequencing of information exchanges among the Parties, including, without limitation, procedures for the use of shared document repositories, electronic databases, or other technology platforms to facilitate the efficient exchange and review of materials.

**Section 4.3 --- Joint Defense Meetings.** The Parties and their Counsel may hold joint defense meetings, whether in person, by telephone, or by videoconference, at such times and with such frequency as the Steering Committee determines appropriate, to discuss defense strategy, share information, coordinate the Common Defense, and address such other matters as may arise in connection with the Litigation or any Related Proceeding. The Steering Committee shall endeavor to provide reasonable advance notice of all joint defense meetings and shall distribute agendas or topics for discussion in advance of such meetings when practicable. Minutes or summaries of joint defense meetings may be prepared at the direction of the Steering Committee and shall be treated as Joint Defense Material subject to all protections and restrictions of this Agreement.

**[ARTICLE V --- COST SHARING]{.underline}**

**Section 5.1 --- Allocation of Joint Defense Costs.** The Parties agree that costs incurred for the common benefit of all Parties in the Joint Defense (\"Joint Defense Costs\"), including, but not limited to, fees and expenses of jointly retained experts, consultants, and e-discovery vendors, costs associated with common document review and production, costs of jointly retained jury consultants, costs of common trial preparation activities, and any other costs that the Steering Committee determines to have been incurred for the common benefit of all Parties, shall be allocated among the Parties as follows:

> \(a\) Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC shall bear fifty percent (50%) of all Joint Defense Costs.
>
> \(b\) The remaining fifty percent (50%) of all Joint Defense Costs shall be divided equally among Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc., Stonebridge Components Corp., and TerraForge Precision, Inc., such that each of Vantage, Stonebridge, and TerraForge shall bear one-third of the remaining fifty percent, or approximately sixteen and sixty-seven one-hundredths percent (16.67%) of total Joint Defense Costs.

The foregoing allocation reflects the Parties\' agreement as to the relative benefit received by each Party from the Common Defense and the relative size and scope of the Claims asserted against each Party.

**Section 5.2 --- Invoicing and Payment.** Joint Defense Costs shall be documented and invoiced on a quarterly basis. The Steering Committee shall review and approve all Joint Defense Costs before they are incurred to the extent reasonably practicable, and in all events shall approve all Joint Defense Costs before any invoices are distributed to the Parties. Invoices for Joint Defense Costs shall be distributed by the Steering Committee to the respective Counsel for each Party, and payment shall be due within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of each invoice. Invoices shall contain a reasonable level of detail sufficient to permit each Party to verify the nature and amount of the costs incurred.

**Section 5.3 --- Individual Costs.** Each Party shall bear its own costs and fees incurred solely for its individual defense, including, but not limited to, the fees and expenses of its own Counsel, the costs of its own individual discovery and motion practice, and any other costs not properly classified as Joint Defense Costs. Nothing in this Agreement shall create any obligation on the part of any Party to reimburse or indemnify any other Party for costs incurred solely in furtherance of such other Party\'s individual defense.

**[ARTICLE VI --- JOINT DEFENSE STEERING COMMITTEE]{.underline}**

**Section 6.1 --- Establishment and Composition.** There is hereby established a Joint Defense Steering Committee (the \"Steering Committee\") to oversee, coordinate, and manage the Common Defense. The Steering Committee shall consist of three (3) members, each of whom shall be a licensed attorney serving as Counsel to a Party in the Litigation. The composition of the Steering Committee shall be as follows:

> \(a\) One (1) permanent seat shall be held by a representative of Pryor Whitfield LLP, Counsel for Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC. The initial holder of such seat shall be Philip S. Pryor, or such other attorney at Pryor Whitfield LLP as may be designated by Kerrigan-Holst from time to time by written notice to all Parties.
>
> \(b\) One (1) seat shall rotate among Counsel for the remaining Parties --- Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc., Stonebridge Components Corp., and TerraForge Precision, Inc. --- on a quarterly basis, in alphabetical order by Party name. The initial rotating member shall be Counsel for Stonebridge Components Corp. (Gould Ramirez LLP), followed by Counsel for TerraForge Precision, Inc. (Pettigrew Shaw PLLC), and then Counsel for Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc. (Alderman & Kessler LLP), with the rotation continuing in such order thereafter.
>
> \(c\) One (1) seat shall be filled by a representative elected by majority vote of all Parties, with each Party receiving one (1) vote. The initial election shall take place within fifteen (15) business days of the Effective Date, and the elected member shall serve for a term of six (6) months, with subsequent elections to be held at the expiration of each term.

**Section 6.2 --- Authority.** The Steering Committee shall have the authority to:

> \(a\) coordinate overall defense strategy in the Litigation and any Related Proceeding, including the identification of common factual and legal issues and the development of unified positions on such issues;
>
> \(b\) direct and manage the exchange of information and Joint Defense Material among the Parties in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement;
>
> \(c\) review and approve Joint Defense Costs before they are incurred, and distribute invoices for such costs to the Parties;
>
> \(d\) retain experts, consultants, e-discovery vendors, jury consultants, and other service providers for the common benefit of the Parties, subject to the decision-making procedures set forth in Section 6.3;
>
> \(e\) schedule, convene, and preside over joint defense meetings of the Parties and their Counsel;
>
> \(f\) serve as the primary point of coordination with the Court on matters affecting all Parties jointly, including the preparation, filing, and argument of joint motions, stipulations, and other filings made on behalf of all Parties; and
>
> \(g\) take such other actions and exercise such other authority as may be reasonably necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of this Agreement and the Common Defense.

**Section 6.3 --- Decision-Making.** Decisions of the Steering Committee shall be made by majority vote of its members, except that the following decisions shall require the unanimous consent of all members of the Steering Committee:

> \(i\) any decision to retain a jointly funded expert witness, including the selection of such expert and the scope of such expert\'s engagement;
>
> \(ii\) any decision to take or oppose a position on behalf of all Parties in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding, including the filing of joint motions, joint briefs, or joint responses; and
>
> \(iii\) any other decision that the Steering Committee, in its discretion, determines to be of sufficient significance to warrant unanimous consent.

In the event of a deadlock on any matter requiring majority vote, the matter shall be referred to a meeting of all Parties and their Counsel for resolution by majority vote of the Parties (with each Party receiving one vote).

**Section 6.4 --- Communications and Reporting.** The Steering Committee shall report to all Parties and their Counsel on material developments in the Common Defense on a regular basis, and in no event less frequently than once per calendar month. Such reports may be made in writing or orally during joint defense meetings and shall address, at a minimum, the status of the Litigation, upcoming deadlines and proceedings, the status of Joint Defense Costs, and any other matters of significance to

**[ARTICLE VII --- WITHDRAWAL]{.underline}**

**Section 7.1 --- Right to Withdraw.** Any Party may withdraw from this Agreement at any time upon thirty (30) calendar days\' prior written notice to all other Parties and their Counsel. Such notice of withdrawal shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions set forth in Section 12.2 of this Agreement and shall identify the withdrawing Party and the effective date of such withdrawal (which shall be the date that is thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of such notice).

**Section 7.2 --- Effect of Withdrawal.** Upon the effective date of a Party\'s withdrawal from this Agreement (i.e., thirty (30) calendar days after delivery of the notice described in Section 7.1):

> \(a\) The withdrawing Party shall immediately cease to be a party to this Agreement and shall no longer be entitled to receive Joint Defense Material from the remaining Parties or to participate in joint defense meetings, Steering Committee proceedings, or any other activities conducted pursuant to this Agreement.
>
> \(b\) The withdrawing Party and its Counsel shall, within fifteen (15) business days of the effective date of withdrawal, return to the disclosing Party or, at the election of the disclosing Party, destroy all Joint Defense Material received from any other Party pursuant to this Agreement, including all copies, summaries, excerpts, and derivative materials. The withdrawing Party shall, within five (5) business days following such return or destruction, certify in writing to all remaining Parties that such return or destruction has been completed and that no copies, summaries, excerpts, or derivative materials have been retained, except as may be required to be retained by applicable law, regulation, or professional obligation.
>
> \(c\) The withdrawing Party and its Counsel shall remain bound by the confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations of this Agreement with respect to any and all Joint Defense Material received prior to the effective date of withdrawal, subject to the survival provisions set forth in Article VIII of this Agreement.
>
> \(d\) The withdrawing Party shall remain responsible for its pro rata share of any Joint Defense Costs that were incurred or approved by the Steering Committee prior to the effective date of withdrawal and that have not yet been paid as of such date.

**Section 7.3 --- No Prejudice to Privilege.** The withdrawal of any Party from this Agreement shall not prejudice, diminish, or waive any privilege, protection, or immunity that attached to Joint Defense Material during the period of such Party\'s participation in this Agreement. The remaining Parties and the withdrawing Party shall cooperate in good faith to assert and maintain all applicable privileges and protections with respect to Joint Defense Material exchanged prior to the effective date of withdrawal.

**[ARTICLE VIII --- SURVIVING OBLIGATIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 8.1 --- Survival of Confidentiality.** The confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations set forth in Article III and Article IV of this Agreement shall survive the termination or expiration of this Agreement, or the withdrawal of any Party from this Agreement, for a period of three (3) years following the date of such termination, expiration, or withdrawal (the \"Survival Period\"). During the Survival Period, the obligations of confidentiality and non-disclosure shall continue in full force and effect as though this Agreement remained in effect, and each Party and its Counsel shall remain bound thereby.

**Section 8.2 --- Obligations During Survival Period.** During the Survival Period, each Party and its Counsel shall continue to treat all Joint Defense Material received during the term of this Agreement as confidential and privileged and shall not disclose, use, reference, or rely upon such material except as permitted under Article III of this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, the use restrictions set forth in Section 3.3 and the third-party disclosure prohibition set forth in Section 3.4 shall remain fully applicable during the Survival Period. Nothing in this Section 8.2 shall be construed to limit the duration of the attorney-client privilege or the work-product doctrine, which shall continue to apply in accordance with their terms and applicable law, regardless of the expiration of the Survival Period.

**[ARTICLE IX --- SEPARATE SETTLEMENT]{.underline}**

**Section 9.1 --- Right to Settle.** Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict, impair, or otherwise limit any Party\'s right to enter into a settlement of any claims asserted against it in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding. Each Party retains sole and absolute discretion over whether to engage in settlement discussions, negotiate settlement terms, or execute any settlement agreement, and no other Party shall have any right to approve, veto, or condition any such settlement.

**Section 9.2 --- Advance Notice of Settlement.** Any Party that intends to negotiate or enter into a settlement with the Plaintiffs, the Consolidated Purchasers Class, or any other party in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding (a \"Settling Party\") shall provide written notice to all other Parties and their Counsel no fewer than forty-five (45) calendar days prior to the anticipated execution of any settlement agreement. Such notice (the \"Settlement Notice\") shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 12.2 and shall include disclosure of all material terms of the proposed settlement, including, without limitation:

> \(a\) the amount or value of the settlement consideration, whether in the form of cash, non-monetary consideration, or a combination thereof;
>
> \(b\) the scope and terms of any release of claims to be granted by the Settling Party or received by the Settling Party;
>
> \(c\) any cooperation provisions obligating the Settling Party to cooperate with the Plaintiffs or any governmental authority in connection with the prosecution of claims against the remaining Parties;
>
> \(d\) any provisions affecting the claims, defenses, rights, or obligations of the remaining Parties, including any provisions that could result in a reduction or offset of the remaining Parties\' liability; and
>
> \(e\) any other terms that are material to the Common Defense or that could reasonably be expected to affect the remaining Parties\' interests in the Litigation.

**Section 9.3 --- Consultation.** The Settling Party and the remaining Parties shall, during the forty-five (45) calendar day notice period specified in Section 9.2, make themselves and their Counsel reasonably available to discuss the impact of the proposed settlement on the Common Defense and the remaining Parties. Such discussions shall be conducted in good faith and shall address, among other things, any modifications to the proposed settlement terms that may be necessary to protect the interests of the remaining Parties. Nothing in this Section 9.3 shall be construed to require the Settling Party to modify or abandon its proposed settlement or to give any remaining Party a veto over such settlement.

**[ARTICLE X --- POST-SETTLEMENT COOPERATION]{.underline}**

**Section 10.1 --- Cooperation Obligation.** A Settling Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make its current and former employees, officers, directors, and agents reasonably available as witnesses to the remaining Parties and their Counsel for a period of eighteen (18) months following the effective date of such Settling Party\'s settlement agreement (the \"Cooperation Period\"). Such cooperation shall include, without limitation, making witnesses available for interviews, deposition preparation sessions, depositions, trial preparation sessions, and trial testimony, at mutually convenient times and locations. The Settling Party shall not be required to take any action that would violate the terms of its settlement agreement or any court order, or that would require the waiver of any privilege held solely by the Settling Party.

**Section 10.2 --- Document Availability.** During the Cooperation Period, the Settling Party shall use commercially reasonable efforts to make documents, records, and data in its possession, custody, or control that are relevant to the remaining Parties\' defense in the Litigation available for inspection and copying by the remaining Parties and their Counsel upon reasonable request and at reasonable times and locations. The costs of any such inspection and copying, including reproduction costs and any costs associated with the retrieval or production of electronically stored information, shall be borne by the Party requesting such cooperation.

**Section 10.3 --- Costs of Cooperation.** The costs of any post-settlement cooperation provided pursuant to this Article X, including, without limitation, reasonable travel expenses, lodging, and other out-of-pocket expenses incurred by witnesses made available by the Settling Party, shall be borne by the Party requesting such cooperation. The Settling Party shall not be required to bear any costs in connection with post-settlement cooperation beyond its own internal administrative costs of facilitating such cooperation.

**[ARTICLE XI --- WAIVER OF CONFLICTS]{.underline}**

**Section 11.1 --- Waiver.** Each Party, on behalf of itself and its Counsel, hereby waives any potential or actual conflict of interest arising from or relating to the participation of any Party or its Counsel in the joint defense established by this Agreement. This waiver encompasses, without limitation, any conflict of interest arising from:

> \(a\) the joint representation of multiple defendants in the Litigation;
>
> \(b\) the exchange of Joint Defense Material among the Parties and their Counsel;
>
> \(c\) the coordination of defense strategy among the Parties and their Counsel;
>
> \(d\) the sharing of confidential or sensitive information that may, in certain circumstances, be adverse to the interests of one or more Parties; and
>
> \(e\) the participation of Counsel for one Party in discussions, meetings, or proceedings in which the interests of such Party may diverge from the interests of another Party.

This waiver is given knowingly and voluntarily by each Party after consultation with independent counsel or after having been afforded the opportunity to consult with independent counsel regarding the terms, conditions, and implications of this waiver.

**Section 11.2 --- Informed Consent.** Each Party acknowledges and agrees that:

> \(a\) the interests of the Parties may diverge as the Litigation progresses, including, without limitation, with respect to the allocation of liability, the assertion of individual defenses, and the terms and conditions of any settlement;
>
> \(b\) information shared under this Agreement could, in theory, be adverse to the interests of one or more Parties or could be used in a manner detrimental to the interests of one or more Parties;
>
> \(c\) the coordination of defense strategy may require compromises or accommodations among the Parties that may not serve the individual interests of each Party equally; and
>
> \(d\) notwithstanding the foregoing, each Party consents to the participation of all Parties and their Counsel in the joint defense established by this Agreement and acknowledges that the benefits of such participation outweigh the risks associated therewith.

**[ARTICLE XII --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**

**Section 12.1 --- No Admission of Liability.** Participation in this Agreement, attendance at joint defense meetings, the sharing of Joint Defense Material, the payment of Joint Defense Costs, or any other action taken pursuant to this Agreement shall not be deemed an admission of liability, wrongdoing, or fault by any Party, nor shall any such action be construed as an admission that any Party engaged in any unlawful conduct as alleged in the Litigation or any Related Proceeding. This Agreement and the actions taken pursuant hereto are undertaken solely for the purpose of facilitating the Common Defense and shall not be admissible in evidence in the Litigation or any other proceeding for any purpose other than to enforce the terms of this Agreement.

**Section 12.2 --- Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, consents, waivers, and other communications required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given and effective:

> \(a\) when delivered personally to the intended recipient or its Counsel;
>
> \(b\) one (1) business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service, with delivery charges prepaid, addressed to the intended recipient or its Counsel at the address set forth on Schedule A hereto; or
>
> \(c\) when sent by electronic mail to the electronic mail address of the intended recipient or its Counsel set forth on Schedule A hereto, with confirmation of receipt by the recipient or its Counsel (such confirmation to be provided by reply electronic mail, read receipt, or other reasonable means).

Any Party may change its address or the address of its Counsel for purposes of notices under this Agreement by providing written notice of such change to all other Parties and their Counsel in accordance with this Section 12.2.

**Section 12.3 --- Governing Law.** This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to its conflicts-of-law principles or any other choice-of-law doctrine that would result in the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction.

**Section 12.4 --- Dispute Resolution.** Any dispute, claim, or controversy arising out of or relating to this Agreement, including, without limitation, any dispute concerning its interpretation, validity, enforceability, breach, or termination, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by JAMS in New York, New York, before a single arbitrator selected in accordance with the JAMS Comprehensive Arbitration Rules and Procedures then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted in the English language. The arbitrator shall have the authority to award any remedy that would be available in a court of competent jurisdiction, including injunctive relief and specific performance. The arbitrator\'s decision shall be final and binding upon the Parties, and judgment upon the award rendered by the arbitrator may be entered in any court of competent jurisdiction. Each Party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees in connection with any such arbitration, unless the arbitrator determines that a different allocation is warranted by the circumstances.

**Section 12.5 --- Entire Agreement.** This Agreement, together with Schedule A attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement among the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous oral or written agreements, discussions, understandings, negotiations, or arrangements among the Parties relating to the subject matter hereof. No Party has relied upon any representation or warranty of any other Party in entering into this Agreement except as expressly set forth herein.

**Section 12.6 --- Amendment.** This Agreement may be amended, modified, or supplemented only by a written instrument executed by all Parties. No amendment, modification, or supplement shall be effective unless it is in writing and signed by a duly authorized representative of each Party. No course of dealing between the Parties shall be deemed to modify or amend any provision of this Agreement.

**Section 12.8 --- Counterparts.** This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of counterparts by facsimile transmission or by electronic means (including transmission of a portable document format (.pdf) image of an executed signature page) shall be deemed to constitute execution and delivery of an original counterpart for all purposes.

**Section 12.9 --- Severability.** If any provision of this Agreement, or the application of any such provision to any person, entity, or circumstance, shall be held by a court of competent jurisdiction or arbitrator to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable in any respect, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect any other provision of this Agreement, and the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and effect. In the event that any provision is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, the Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace such provision with a valid, legal, and enforceable provision that, to the greatest extent possible, achieves the intended purpose and economic effect of the original provision.

**Section 12.10 --- Additional Parties.** Additional defendants in the Litigation, or other persons or entities with a common legal interest in the Common Defense, may become parties to this Agreement upon the prior written consent of all existing Parties and the execution of a joinder agreement in a form approved by the Steering Committee. IN THE UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT FOR THE NORTHERN DISTRICT OF ILLINOIS EASTERN DIVISION

\ 

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **IN RE INDUSTRIAL FASTENERS ANTITRUST LITIGATION**   **Case No. 1:23-cv-04871**
  ----------------------------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  This Document Relates To:                             Hon. Margaret R. Tanaka

  ALL DIRECT PURCHASER ACTIONS                          
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

\ 

**CONSOLIDATED CLASS ACTION COMPLAINT**

\ 

Filed by the Consolidated Purchasers Class, by and through undersigned counsel, on behalf of all direct purchasers of industrial fasteners, against Defendants Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC; Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc.; Stonebridge Components Corp.; and TerraForge Precision, Inc.

\ 

Plaintiffs Midwest Structural Supply Co.; Great Lakes Assembly Partners, Inc.; Heritage Infrastructure Group, LLC; Capitol Fabrication & Engineering, Inc.; and Southeastern Building Components, LLC (collectively, \"Plaintiffs\" or \"Named Plaintiffs\"), individually and on behalf of all others similarly situated, by their undersigned attorneys, bring this Consolidated Class Action Complaint against Defendants Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC (\"Kerrigan-Holst\"); Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc. (\"Vantage\"); Stonebridge Components Corp. (\"Stonebridge\"); and TerraForge Precision, Inc. (\"TerraForge\") (collectively, \"Defendants\"), and allege as follows based upon personal knowledge, investigation of counsel, publicly available information, and information and belief:

**[I. NATURE OF THE ACTION]{.underline}**

1\. This is a civil antitrust action brought under Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1, and Section 4 of the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. § 15, seeking treble damages, injunctive relief, costs of suit, and reasonable attorneys\' fees. This action arises from a conspiracy among the Defendants --- the dominant manufacturers and suppliers of industrial fasteners in the United States --- to unlawfully fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize prices; rig bids in connection with large-volume procurement contracts; and allocate customers and geographic territories for the sale of industrial fasteners throughout the United States.

2\. Plaintiffs are direct purchasers of industrial fasteners --- including but not limited to bolts, nuts, screws, rivets, anchors, pins, studs, washers, and related threaded and non-threaded hardware used in manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, and original equipment manufacturing (\"OEM\") applications --- who purchased such products directly from one or more of the Defendants during the period from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2022 (the \"Class Period\"). Plaintiffs purchased industrial fasteners for use in their own businesses or for resale to downstream customers, paying prices that were artificially inflated as a direct result of the Defendants\' unlawful conduct alleged herein.

3\. Defendants are competing manufacturers and suppliers of industrial fasteners who, beginning no later than January 1, 2018, and continuing through at least December 31, 2022, entered into and carried out a continuing conspiracy, agreement, and understanding to fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize prices for industrial fasteners; to rig bids on large-volume procurement contracts, including government and quasi-governmental contracts; and to allocate customers and geographic territories for the sale of industrial fasteners in the United States. This conspiracy constitutes a per se violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1. Defendants\' conspiracy was effectuated through direct communications among their senior executives, pricing directors, and regional sales managers, including at meetings held under the auspices of the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association (\"IFTA\"), at industry conferences, and through private bilateral contacts among Defendants\' personnel.

4\. As a direct and proximate result of Defendants\' unlawful conspiracy, Plaintiffs and the members of the proposed Class (defined below) paid artificially inflated, supra-competitive prices for industrial fasteners throughout the Class Period. Plaintiffs and the Class have been injured in their business and property as a result of these overcharges, and they are entitled to recover treble damages, together with the costs of this action and reasonable attorneys\' fees, pursuant to Section 4 of the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. § 15. On information and belief, the aggregate overcharges suffered by the Class during the Class Period exceed \$750 million.

**[II. JURISDICTION AND VENUE]{.underline}**

5\. This Court has subject-matter jurisdiction over this action pursuant to 28 U.S.C. §§ 1331 and 1337(a), which confer original jurisdiction over civil actions arising under the laws of the United States, including the federal antitrust laws, and pursuant to Sections 4 and 16 of the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 15 and 26, which provide a private right of action for persons injured by violations of the federal antitrust laws. This action arises under Section 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1, and Plaintiffs seek damages, injunctive relief, and other remedies authorized by the Clayton Act.

6\. This Court has personal jurisdiction over each Defendant. Each Defendant has transacted substantial business within this judicial District, has directed sales of industrial fasteners into this District, has maintained offices, agents, or representatives within this District, and has committed overt acts in furtherance of the conspiracy alleged herein within this District. Defendant Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC is headquartered in Chicago, Illinois, within this District, and has its principal place of business here. Defendants Vantage, Stonebridge, and TerraForge each sold substantial quantities of industrial fasteners to purchasers located within this District during the Class Period, participated in meetings and communications in furtherance of the conspiracy that occurred within this District, and otherwise have sufficient minimum contacts with the State of Illinois and this District to satisfy constitutional due process requirements. Each Defendant has purposefully availed itself of the laws and markets of this District and could reasonably anticipate being haled into court here.

7\. Venue is proper in this District pursuant to Section 12 of the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. § 22, and 28 U.S.C. § 1391(b) and (c). A substantial part of the events or omissions giving rise to the claims asserted herein occurred in this District, including conspiratorial meetings at industry events held in Chicago, Illinois; pricing decisions made by Kerrigan-Holst at its Chicago headquarters; and sales of industrial fasteners to Class Members located in this District. In addition, Defendant Kerrigan-Holst resides in this District by virtue of its principal place of business, and each Defendant is subject to personal jurisdiction in this District with respect to the claims asserted herein.

**[III. THE PARTIES]{.underline}**

**A. Plaintiffs and the Proposed Class**

8\. The Named Plaintiffs are identified direct purchasers of industrial fasteners who represent a cross-section of the industries served by Defendants, including the manufacturing, construction, and infrastructure sectors. Each Named Plaintiff purchased industrial fasteners directly from one or more of the Defendants during the Class Period, and each paid prices that were artificially inflated as a result of the conspiracy alleged herein. The Named Plaintiffs are:

> \(a\) **Midwest Structural Supply Co.** is an Illinois corporation with its principal place of business in Naperville, Illinois. Midwest Structural Supply is a distributor and end-user of industrial fasteners, purchasing large quantities of bolts, nuts, screws, and rivets directly from Kerrigan-Holst and Stonebridge for use in structural steel fabrication projects throughout the Midwest. During the Class Period, Midwest Structural Supply purchased approximately \$18.4 million in industrial fasteners directly from Defendants.
>
> \(b\) **Great Lakes Assembly Partners, Inc.** is a Michigan corporation with its principal place of business in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Great Lakes Assembly Partners is a contract manufacturer that purchases industrial fasteners directly from Kerrigan-Holst, Vantage, and TerraForge for use in automotive and heavy-equipment assembly operations. During the Class Period, Great Lakes Assembly Partners purchased approximately \$12.7 million in industrial fasteners directly from Defendants.
>
> \(c\) **Heritage Infrastructure Group, LLC** is a Virginia limited liability company with its principal place of business in Arlington, Virginia. Heritage Infrastructure Group is a general contractor engaged in public infrastructure and transportation projects that purchases industrial fasteners, including military-specification and government-standard fasteners, directly from Kerrigan-Holst and Stonebridge. During the Class Period, Heritage Infrastructure Group purchased approximately \$9.2 million in industrial fasteners directly from Defendants.
>
> \(d\) **Capitol Fabrication & Engineering, Inc.** is a Pennsylvania corporation with its principal place of business in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. Capitol Fabrication is a specialty fabricator that purchases industrial fasteners directly from Stonebridge and Vantage for use in commercial building construction and bridge fabrication. During the Class Period, Capitol Fabrication purchased approximately \$6.8 million in industrial fasteners directly from Defendants.
>
> \(e\) **Southeastern Building Components, LLC** is a Georgia limited liability company with its principal place of business in Atlanta, Georgia. Southeastern Building Components is a distributor and installer of commercial building components that purchases industrial fasteners directly from Vantage and TerraForge. During the Class Period, Southeastern Building Components purchased approximately \$5.1 million in industrial fasteners directly from Defendants.

9\. Plaintiffs bring this action on behalf of themselves and all others similarly situated pursuant to Federal Rules of Civil Procedure 23(a) and 23(b)(3). This action is properly maintainable as a class action because it satisfies all of the prerequisites of Rule 23, as more fully set forth in Section VII below.

10\. **Class Definition.** Plaintiffs seek to represent the following Class:

> All persons and entities that purchased industrial fasteners --- including but not limited to bolts, nuts, screws, rivets, anchors, pins, studs, washers, and related threaded or non-threaded hardware products --- directly from any Defendant or any subsidiary, affiliate, predecessor, successor, or agent thereof, in the United States, during the period from January 1, 2018 through December 31, 2022 (the \"Class\" or \"Class Members\").
>
> Excluded from the Class are: (i) Defendants and their respective parent companies, subsidiaries, and affiliates; (ii) any co-conspirators identified herein or hereafter identified; (iii) federal and state governmental entities; (iv) any judicial officer presiding over this action and the members of his or her immediate family and judicial staff; and (v) any person or entity who timely and validly opts out of the Class.

**B. Defendants.**

11\. **Kerrigan-Holst Manufacturing Group, LLC** (\"Kerrigan-Holst\") is a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal place of business and corporate headquarters located at 311 West Wacker Drive, 42nd Floor, Chicago, Illinois 60606. Kerrigan-Holst is the largest participant in the United States industrial fasteners market by revenue. Kerrigan-Holst manufactures and sells a broad range of industrial fasteners, including standard and specialty bolts, nuts, screws, rivets, anchors, studs, and related hardware, from manufacturing facilities located in Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Alabama. During the Class Period, Kerrigan-Holst\'s industrial fasteners sales in the United States exceeded \$2.1 billion. Based on publicly available data and industry analyses, Kerrigan-Holst holds an estimated market share of approximately 35% of the relevant market defined herein. Kerrigan-Holst sold industrial fasteners to purchasers located in all fifty states during the Class Period and is a member of the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association.

12\. **Vantage Industrial Solutions, Inc.** (\"Vantage\") is a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal place of business and corporate headquarters located at 4200 Tryon Ridge Parkway, Suite 900, Charlotte, North Carolina 28217. Vantage is a mid-tier manufacturer of industrial fasteners, producing standard bolts, nuts, screws, and specialty engineered fastener systems from manufacturing facilities in North Carolina, South Carolina, Tennessee, and Georgia. During the Class Period, Vantage\'s industrial fasteners sales in the United States were approximately \$640 million. Based on publicly available data and industry analyses, Vantage holds an estimated market share of approximately 11% of the relevant market defined herein. Vantage sold industrial fasteners to purchasers located throughout the United States during the Class Period and is a member of the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association.

13\. **Stonebridge Components Corp.** (\"Stonebridge\") is a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Ohio, with its principal place of business and corporate headquarters located at 1020 Lakeside Avenue East, Cleveland, Ohio 44114. Stonebridge is a specialty fastener supplier with particular strength in high-specification, aerospace-grade, and military-specification fasteners, as well as standard industrial fasteners. Stonebridge operates manufacturing facilities in Ohio, Michigan, and New York. During the Class Period, Stonebridge\'s industrial fasteners sales in the United States were approximately \$480 million. Based on publicly available data and industry analyses, Stonebridge holds an estimated market share of approximately 8% of the relevant market defined herein. Stonebridge sold industrial fasteners to purchasers located throughout the United States during the Class Period and is a member of the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association.

14\. **TerraForge Precision, Inc.** (\"TerraForge\") is a corporation organized under the laws of the State of Texas, with its principal place of business and corporate headquarters located at 8700 Westpark Drive, Suite 400, Houston, Texas 77063. TerraForge is a regional competitor in the industrial fasteners market with particular strength in the Gulf Coast, Southwest, and energy-sector markets. TerraForge manufactures standard and engineered fasteners from facilities in Texas, Louisiana, and Oklahoma. During the Class Period, TerraForge\'s industrial fasteners sales in the United States were approximately \$390 million. Based on publicly available data and industry analyses, TerraForge holds an estimated market share of approximately 7% of the relevant market defined herein. TerraForge sold industrial fasteners to purchasers located throughout the United States during the Class Period and is a member of the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association.

15\. At all times relevant to this Complaint, each Defendant acted as a principal or agent of, or was otherwise authorized to act on behalf of, each other Defendant with respect to the acts, conduct, and transactions alleged herein. Each Defendant was engaged in interstate commerce, or in activities substantially affecting interstate commerce, within the meaning of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1, and the Clayton Act, 15 U.S.C. § 15.

**[IV. AGENTS AND CO-CONSPIRATORS]{.underline}**

16\. Various persons and entities not named as Defendants herein participated as co-conspirators in the violations alleged in this Complaint. These co-conspirators include, but are not limited to, unnamed senior executives, vice presidents, regional sales managers, pricing directors, and other employees and agents at each Defendant who, acting within the scope of their authority, directed, authorized, carried out, or facilitated the conspiratorial agreements described herein. In addition, upon information and belief, certain other manufacturers and suppliers of industrial fasteners not yet identified may have participated in one or more aspects of the conspiracy and may be added as defendants or co-conspirators upon further discovery and investigation.

17\. Whenever in this Complaint reference is made to any act, deed, statement, or communication by any Defendant, such reference shall be deemed to include the acts, deeds, statements, and communications of the Defendant\'s officers, directors, employees, agents, and representatives, whether acting individually or in concert with others, and whether acting within the actual or apparent scope of their authority with such Defendant.

**[V. THE RELEVANT MARKET AND INTERSTATE COMMERCE]{.underline}**

**A. Product Market**

18\. The relevant product market for purposes of this action is the manufacture and sale of industrial fasteners in the United States. As used herein, \"industrial fasteners\" means bolts, nuts, screws, rivets, anchors, pins, studs, washers, and related threaded and non-threaded hardware products used in manufacturing, construction, infrastructure, aerospace, automotive, energy, and OEM applications. Industrial fasteners are manufactured from steel, stainless steel, aluminum, brass, titanium, and other metals and alloys, in a wide range of sizes, grades, specifications, and finishes. The product market includes both standard catalog fasteners and custom-engineered or specialty fasteners manufactured to customer-specific or military specifications.

19\. Industrial fasteners are essential, non-substitutable inputs for their end-use applications. There are no practicable alternatives to industrial fasteners for the structural joining, clamping, and assembly functions that fasteners perform. Purchasers cannot substitute adhesives, welding, or other joining methods for the vast majority of applications requiring industrial fasteners without incurring prohibitive costs, unacceptable performance trade-offs, or violations of engineering standards, building codes, and regulatory requirements. The cross-elasticity of demand between industrial fasteners and alternative joining methods is negligible. A hypothetical monopolist of industrial fasteners could profitably impose a small but significant and non-transitory increase in price (\"SSNIP\") without losing substantial sales to alternative products.

**B. Geographic Market**

20\. The relevant geographic market is the United States, including all fifty states, the District of Columbia, and the territories and possessions of the United States. During the Class Period, Defendants manufactured, marketed, distributed, and sold industrial fasteners throughout the United States. Purchasers of industrial fasteners generally source their requirements from domestic manufacturers and suppliers, and the costs of importing fasteners from foreign sources --- including tariffs, transportation costs, lead times, and quality-assurance requirements --- limit the competitive constraint exerted by foreign suppliers on domestic pricing. Defendants set prices on a national basis, subject to regional variations consistent with the customer and territory allocation agreement alleged herein.

**C. Interstate Commerce**

21\. During the Class Period, each Defendant manufactured and sold industrial fasteners in a continuous and uninterrupted flow of interstate commerce. Each Defendant manufactured fasteners in one or more states and shipped those products across state lines to customers located in other states. Each Defendant\'s sales of industrial fasteners involved, and the conspiracy alleged herein substantially affected, interstate commerce within the meaning of the Sherman Act. The activities of Defendants alleged herein had a direct, substantial, and reasonably foreseeable effect on interstate commerce in the United States.

**D. Market Structure**

22\. The United States industrial fasteners market is highly concentrated. During the Class Period, the four Defendants collectively held an estimated combined market share of approximately 61% of the relevant market by revenue. The total addressable market for industrial fasteners sold in the United States during the Class Period was approximately \$5.8 billion annually, reflecting steady demand driven by manufacturing output, construction activity, and infrastructure investment. The Herfindahl-Hirschman Index (\"HHI\") for the relevant market, calculated on the basis of the four Defendants\' market shares alone, exceeds 1,500, indicating a concentrated market susceptible to coordinated behavior. When the market shares of additional, smaller competitors are included, the concentration remains well above levels at which coordinated effects are presumed likely.

23\. Several structural characteristics of the industrial fasteners market facilitate collusion among competitors and make the conspiracy alleged herein both plausible and sustainable. These characteristics include, but are not limited to:

> \(a\) **Standardized Products.** Industrial fasteners are manufactured to common specifications, including ASTM, SAE, ISO, and military standards. The standardization of products across manufacturers means that purchasers view competing suppliers\' products as highly interchangeable, which in turn means that prices --- rather than product differentiation --- are the primary competitive variable. This high degree of product homogeneity facilitates price coordination, as conspirators need only agree on price levels rather than on a complex array of product attributes.
>
> \(b\) **High Barriers to Entry.** Entry into the industrial fasteners market requires substantial capital investment in cold-heading, hot-forging, threading, heat-treatment, and finishing equipment; quality-assurance and testing facilities; engineering expertise; certifications (including ISO 9001, AS9100, and IATF 16949); established supply chains for raw materials; and customer relationships developed over years. These barriers inhibit new entrants from constraining the pricing behavior of incumbent manufacturers and thereby reduce the competitive discipline that potential entry would otherwise impose.
>
> \(c\) **Inelastic Demand.** Demand for industrial fasteners is highly inelastic because fasteners represent a small fraction of the total cost of the end products and structures into which they are incorporated, and because there are no practicable substitutes. Purchasers absorb price increases rather than curtail purchases, which makes price-fixing profitable.
>
> \(d\) **Limited Product Differentiation.** Although some specialty fasteners command premium pricing, the majority of industrial fasteners sold in the United States are commodity-grade products with limited differentiation among manufacturers. Defendants\' products are largely fungible, enabling purchasers to switch among suppliers on the basis of price --- a characteristic that, absent collusion, would intensify price competition but that, in the presence of a conspiracy, facilitates supra-competitive pricing because each conspirator knows that its co-conspirators will not undercut the agreed-upon price.
>
> \(e\) **Regular Interaction Among Competitors.** Defendants\' executives and sales personnel regularly interacted at meetings and events organized by the Industrial Fasteners Trade Association (\"IFTA\"), at trade shows such as the International Fastener Expo and the National Industrial Fastener and Mill Supply Expo, and through other industry forums. These regular interactions provided opportunities for communication and coordination of the conspiracy alleged herein.

**[VI. FACTUAL ALLEGATIONS --- THE CONSPIRACY]{.underline}**

**A. Overview of the Conspiracy**

24\. Beginning no later than January 1, 2018, and continuing through at least December 31, 2022, Defendants and their co-conspirators entered into and participated in a continuing agreement, understanding, and concert of action in unreasonable restraint of interstate trade and commerce, in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1. The objects of the conspiracy were to fix, raise, maintain, and stabilize prices for industrial fasteners sold in the United States; to rig bids on large-volume and government procurement contracts for industrial fasteners; and to allocate customers and geograph
